title: SIU probes death of man hit by Taser
article: It will be some time before investigators know why Jeffrey Mark Marreel died more than an hour after being hit by a Taser during a violent confrontation with five OPP officers Monday.

Results of an autopsy performed yesterday at Hamilton General Hospital were inconclusive, a spokesman for Ontario's Special Investigations Unit probing his death said yesterday. More tests have been ordered.

Unconfirmed reports suggest Marreel was swinging a weapon such as a piece of pipe or piece of wood when police approached. The OPP, which is not allowed to comment on the incident once the SIU has invoked its mandate to investigate, would only say in a statement Monday that officers were dealing with a "combative" person.
Although no date has been set, there will be a mandatory inquest into Marreel's death because his death occurred in police custody.
Marreel, who was 36, was known to have a drug problem and may have been using drugs when he encountered Norfolk OPP officers sent to the hamlet of Fisher's Glen on Lake Erie south of Delhi.
Although he grew up around Delhi and his parents and other family live there, Marreel had no fixed address but moved around staying with friends.
SIU spokesman John Yoannou said yesterday the OPP received a call from a resident near Fisher's Glen reporting a person behaving suspiciously in the area.
The officers encountered Marreel in the middle of the intersection of Fisher's Glen Road and Front Road at 10:30 a.m.
The OPP said in a statement the officers encountered a "combative" man and a Taser was used to subdue him.
Marreel was placed under arrest and taken to the Norfolk OPP detachment in Simcoe. He collapsed at the detachment at 11:30 a.m., an hour after he'd been hit by a Taser.
Marreel was given first aid by police until paramedics arrived and transferred him to Norfolk General Hospital nearby where he was pronounced dead at 12:30 p.m.
Marreel's father, Noel, told Canadian Press his son had a drug problem.
"I suspect he was (using drugs)," the elder Marreel said.
He also said his son had just broken up with his girlfriend in the last month and lost his job two weeks ago. "He was on a down cycle."

The SIU -- a provincial agency which investigates incidents between civilians and police which involve serious injury, sexual assault or death -- has appealed for any witnesses to contact them at 1-800-787-8529.
